brief.subject: FMCSA pulls 133 ELDs; Mexico tariff threat; LA rail dwell
brief.headline: FMCSA Revokes 133 ELDs as Mexico Tariff Threat Clouds Cross-Border Freight
brief.dek: Regulators pull 133 logging devices, Trump threatens to double Mexico tariffs, and LA port volume and rail delays climb together.
brief.lede: FMCSA removed 133 electronic logging devices from its approved registry, citing fraud and compliance failures. Carriers should confirm their ELD is still listed.

sections.heading: 133 ELDs Pulled From Registry
bullets: 133 devices: FMCSA struck them from its approved ELD list in a fraud crackdown.
Regulators cited widespread compliance failures and evidence of fraud behind the removals.
Running a revoked device can put your logs and roadside inspections at risk, so verify your unit's status now.

sections.heading: Mexico Tariffs Could Double
bullets: Doubled tariffs: Trump threatened them on Mexican imports unless Mexico stops migrant caravans.
Effective immediately: the president said the higher levies would hit if Mexico fails to act.
Cross-border and border-lane carriers could see freight volumes swing quickly if the threat is carried out.

sections.heading: LA Booms While Rail Backs Up
bullets: Over 1 million TEUs: Los Angeles topped that mark for a second straight month in a record October.
5%: October cargo ran ahead of 2025, keeping Southern California drayage demand strong.
Over nine days: rail-bound containers are sitting idle at the port, per Executive Director Gene Seroka.
Long rail dwell can push more boxes toward trucks and tie up chassis and terminal time.

sections.heading: Dash Cams and Nuclear Verdicts
bullets: $604M: a recent verdict has defense attorneys warning fleets about gaps in AI-only dash cams.
Plaintiff lawyers hunt for systemic failure, not just crash facts, says defense attorney Doug Marcello.
Risky driving a camera recorded but nobody reviewed can become evidence against a small fleet.

sections.heading: Trade Policy Gets Murkier
bullets: Both chambers: Democrats' midterm wins add uncertainty to the trade outlook.
Three bills in Congress would sharply limit presidential tariff power if they become law.
Trans-Pacific ocean rates stay elevated as imports ease from a near-record peak, a signal for port-lane demand.
